survey: A saguaro-style cactus stands straight up in a sand dune, with rocks around it. The camera is a little above the ground and slightly to the front-left. The main trunk is a vertical cylinder with a rounded top and a pink flower on the crown. Its ribs run straight up and crowd together toward the left and right edges, which is what ribs on a curved surface should do. The ribs meet at the crown, and the flower is seen slightly from the side and above. The left arm comes out of the trunk's left side a little behind the trunk's front surface, bends, and rises as a vertical cylinder; its ribs crowd at its edges too. The right arm comes forward out of the trunk's right side and overlaps it. Its ribs run along the horizontal part and turn upward through the elbow, and the upright part is parallel to the trunk. Both arms tilt away from the viewer the same way as the trunk, so the verticals stay vertical. The spines sit on the ridges of the ribs and stick out sideways where the surface turns away. The trunk goes into the sand at a slight angle under a small mound, which matches how the gently sloping ground is drawn. The rocks and shadows are seen from the same slightly raised view.
